text:
alex: Heads-up — ran into a weird case where server-side splitting of an oversized embeds request is reordering pieces on the downstream GPU pool. Observed client sent 3 docs [A,B,C] but result assembly came back B,A,C. Anyone seen order shuffling during routing/split?
priya: yikes. do you have request/response headers + sample ids?
alex: pasting sanitized headers. note: we used server_split=true and no sequence header:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
X-Client-Id: app-42
X-Embed-Split: server
body: {"inputs": ["A","B","C"]}  # oversized -> auto-split into 2 subrequests
```
responses had: subreq-1 -> ids [B], subreq-2 -> ids [A,C]
colin: hmm that indicates our splitter is grouping by size then shuffling by tenant-shard. order preservation wasn't a strict guarantee for server-side splits. we assumed consumers only cared about ids mapping, not positional order.
jeanne: that's a UX problem. several downstream customers rely on stable ordering (embedding arrays map -> original docs). Can we add a deterministic `sequence_index` header per chunk so clients can reassemble? and show mapping in console so users can debug splits?
colin: agree on sequence_index header. two options: 1) guarantee preserving original order when we split (more expensive because we'd need to serialize across shards) or 2) emit metadata so client/console can reassemble cheaply.
priya: leaning 2. low-risk and cheaper. add headers: `X-Embed-Chunk-Id`, `X-Embed-Chunk-Seq` and `X-Embed-Orig-Idxs` (comma list). runtime can populate and telemetry can trace join.
alex: that would work. also need to think quota attribution: right now quotas are per-embedding-unit (dims-based) but our splitter charges per-subrequest bytes. customers will be confused if unit counts don't sum to original. we should surface both: charged_units and original_estimated_units.
jeanne: console change: in the 'Requests' tab show a split preview card when a split occurs: visual mapping from original indices -> subrequests, charged units per subrequest, and latency per shard. small mock: 
```json
{
  "original_count": 3,
  "subrequests": [
    {"id": "sr-1", "orig_idxs": [0], "charged_units": "0.5U"},
    {"id": "sr-2", "orig_idxs": [1,2], "charged_units": "1.2U"}
  ]
}
```
colin: implementation notes: need to update router to tag per-chunk metadata and ensure that fallback routes (e.g., cheaper quantized variant) preserve those headers. also add an invariant test in the ingress e2e suite that reassembly by `X-Embed-Chunk-Seq` yields original order.
priya: telemetry: emit `embed.split` event with fields: `num_subreq`, `orig_count`, `charged_total_units`, `reassembly_ok` boolean. that'll let Optimize recommend client_ vs server_split.
alex: what about rollouts? I'd prefer feature-flagging the new headers and console card behind `split-debugging-v1` and enable canary for 5% tenants.
jeanne: agreed. add a console config toggle so support can switch on for specific customers when debugging.
colin: one more gotcha — SDKs that currently rely on positional results will break when server_split default is turned on. we should change SDKs to: if response contains `X-Embed-Chunk-Seq` metadata, reassemble before returning to user; otherwise fallback to legacy behavior. bump minor version and include migration notes.
alex: i'll open an RFC for the header names + telemetry schema. quick ask: can infra-bot run a canary deployment once we have a build?
ingress-bot: deploy request queued: canary/split-debugging-v1 -> shardset-canary-3; ETA ~ 12m. logs will be posted to #deploy-notifications.
priya: awesome. thanks. I'll draft console mockups and telemetry fields and drop in this thread for review.
jeanne: when we enable canary, let's also add an alert if `reassembly_ok=false` > 0.1% of requests — we can auto-roll back.
colin: sounds good. i'll add unit/e2e tests and a small runtime perf guard so preserving order (if we ever opt for option1) has a SLO impact flag.
alex: thanks team. filing RFC link shortly.
